newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Pernas projects sharp rise in profit.
newsitem.headline: Pernas projects sharp rise in profit.

text.p: Malaysian hotel and property firm Pernas International Holdings Bhd said on Monday its pre-tax profit was expected to rise to 500 million ringgit in the financial year 2000/01.
It announced that for the year ended January 31, 1997, the company's pre-tax profit was 134 million ringgit against 70.74 million ringgit in the previous year.

Pernas said in a statement that with steps undertaken as part of the second phase of a restructuring exercise "the group is confident that it will attain the 500 million ringgit pre-tax profit by the financial year 2000/01".
Under the second phase of the restructuring, Pernas is planning to list its plantations and hotel and properties units.
These would add significant cash flows to the group, whose cash flows have improved substantially due to disposal of some of its assets recently.

Pernas has raised 868 million ringgit from sale of assets considered "non-strategic". This included sale of 10.2 percent stake in MNI Holdings, one of the country's leading insurers, for 364 million ringgit.
"The group will continue to dispose of its non-strategic assets in order to be more focused in its core businesses," the Pernas statement said.
